- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially sentiment > 0.8) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (sentiment < 0.5) — model is overly optimistic or fails to recognize downward pressure.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to recent spikes, then forecasts a sharp drop — but true mean reversion is slower and less pronounced.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often peaks 1–2 days too early, then drops — true price moves more gradually.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model overfits short-term sentiment swings, leading to erratic forecasts.
- Model tends to overpredict mid-term (10–20d) prices after a spike, then underpredict later (20–30d) — suggesting diminishing momentum or policy-induced cooling.
- Avoid extrapolating sentiment trends beyond 3–5 days — sentiment often reverses or stabilizes before model adjusts.
